prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this existing ZANKII Lunar Light game design board with MINIMAL changes. Preserve the entire composition, moon, mountains, navy background, thin lavender platform outlines, fonts, text, menu cards, layout, Fat Wave character silhouette and zigzag trail. This is a precise cleanup requested by the user; do not redesign.

CHANGE 1 — CHARACTER PRIMARY COLOR: In both the small flying Fat Wave character at top and the enlarged Fat Wave preview bottom right, replace the vivid blue outer shell with a clearly DARK BLUE, approximately #183B8C. Keep the secondary inner disk and small secondary details VIOLET #7D00FF, unchanged. Keep a narrow subtle blue edge highlight so the dark shell remains legible against navy, but the body fill itself MUST visibly read as dark royal/navy blue, substantially darker than the input. Change the small blue color swatch in the bottom legend to the same dark blue and change its text from '1 BLUE' to '1 DARK BLUE'. Keep '2 VIOLET' and the violet swatch unchanged. Match the small icon in the first menu card thumbnail too.

CHANGE 2 — CLEAN OBSTACLES: Remove overlapping and nested spike/crystal shapes and visual artifacts. Every hazard must have a clean single outline and stand separately, with visible breathing room between neighboring hazards. In particular simplify the tangled pair of overlapping crystals underneath the top platform around x=45% of the image; show one plain triangle and one clean separate faceted diamond crystal instead. Simplify the overlapping bottom-right crystal cluster around x=85% of the image: replace it with a single modest faceted crystal plus a separate triangle at a clear distance. Under the floating platform at upper-right use just three clean separate hazards, no layered duplicate tips. Remove the small decorative diamond pendants embedded inside vertical walls of the large central bottom platform (they resemble spikes within spikes and clutter the silhouette); leave those faces plain with subtle thin panel lines. Remove stray floating fragments and slivers along platform outlines. Keep the overall platform geometry, obstacle placement rhythm and corridor open space the same. Keep the original moderate number of hazards, but fewer where cleanup calls for it. The faceting inside the remaining crystals may be restrained, without extra small spikes within their outlines. Apply the same cleanup to the tiny menu card previews. Preserve all other image elements exactly. Result should look almost the same as the input, only a darker blue character and simpler, tidier hazards.
